prompts.text: RE-OPEN dispatch: the quarantine cited a panel-template CELL CAP that an audit proved does not exist (GolayDecoderBlock is a 7-cell panel block, status done). Finish the block; the job is placement/integration, not DSP.

notes:
RE-OPENED. NOT done, but the quarantine's wall is gone and the real blocker is measured to the word.

THE CELL CAP WAS FICTION, and so were two of the three 'walls'. engine/panel_pnr.py has no cell_count check; its only count limit caps how many BLOCKS may be panel-backed. Measured extra fact the audit did not have: GolayDecoderBlock -- the block that refutes the cap -- fails the SAME template with a TypeError, because the RX shape writes Varicode-specific params into blk.params. The template was broken for both, for neither reason the quarantine gave. The 'no single-face ring' test searched RINGS (every edge the same way round a cycle), which is not the fabric. The 'template rejects this block' test asserted only that SOMETHING raised.

NOW GREEN: a new _apply_self_contained_template places ALL SEVEN cells from the block's own default_layout with the controller pinned on x1_out, draws the input/return/egress corridors and derives the push-read descriptors -- 0 DRC errors, 0 warnings, and the build binds every program to its placed cell. placekyt/tests 1219 passed; the LZ4, Golay, Varicode, panel-refresh and GRC-binding suites 638 passed.

THE SUBSTRATE RULE, read off a simkyt trace rather than inferred: a word leaves on its SOURCE cell's face, and every cell it then arrives at forwards it on THAT CELL'S OWN face. Each cell has exactly ONE outgoing walk. The straight-line 'ray' model is FALSE, and believing it is how this block got a row that places clean, builds clean, passes DRC -- and HANGS, because the router faces west into an emit cell facing east and the word ping-pongs. This is now INV-48 root cause C.

FAN-OUT IS NOT THE WALL, checked against the library before saying so: LMSEqualizerBlock ships with fan-out 6 and 5 backward edges, FFT64Block with 4 and 6 -- both strictly worse than this block's (4, 3), both done. They win by putting a cell's targets CONSECUTIVELY along one walk and by authoring in-program FACE FLIPS (DataWord(is_face=True) + MOVE [FACE]), which cost 2 instructions + 1 data word per extra direction.

THE REMAINING BLOCKER, with arithmetic: a ring over cells 0..5 with the controller OFF the ring satisfies all 14 inter-cell edges in the natural order (exhaustive). The leftover emit->controller edge needs a face flip; the emit cell has 2 free words against the 3 a flip costs (token has 1). Exhaustive over every 4x2..7x2 fold with per-cell budgets: nothing every cell can afford. The way through is measured too -- the per-byte set_addr is redundant (the controller's write entry auto-increments its own wraddr; equivalent to the golden on 19 payloads) and frees exactly 3 words -- but it changes the program the match copy is PROVEN on, so it needs its own silicon re-verification and was not taken. Doing that is the next agent's whole job.

FOUR SILENT TOOLCHAIN BUGS FOUND AND FIXED, each of which would corrupt any future block of this shape: (1) router._find_output_target returned the target's DEFAULT entry for a port carrying both a WRITE and a JUMP, so one cell driving several entries of a companion fired them all at the first; (2) router._fixup_write_instructions' sink fallback rewrote EVERY WRITE/JUMP in the exit cell to the port hop, aiming the panel protocol at x16_out -- now honours RAW_OUTPUT_HOPS via a new BlockDefinition.raw_output_hops; (3) build._apply_output_port_routes lacked the RAW_OUTPUT_HOPS guard its sibling _apply_routes has; (4) build._patch_one_handoff matches by destination REGISTER alone and takes the lowest-addressed hit, so a cell driving two different cells' registers that share a number patches the wrong instruction.

ALSO CORRECTED: the block declared no output_cell_id(), so the port map put its output on the CONTROLLER; and its docstring repeated the false 'x1 is one bit wide' claim -- x1 is a SERDES, width:1 is a PIN COUNT, and the panel pushes full 16-bit words through it. The prior factory record's 'a data word cannot transit a 1-bit port' is wrong for the same reason.

TESTS: 41 passed, 4 skipped. The three test_placement_wall_* gates are gone and LAYER 5's header records what each got wrong. New gates pin the placement, the build binding, the EXACT set of unroutable edges and the flip budget -- the last two fail the day the gap closes -- and the written-and-ready end-to-end decode test is skipped until then.
